Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: Denial of Service via use-after-free in nfsd
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

nfsd: hold cl_lock in client_has_openowners()

client_has_openowners() walks clp->cl_openowners and reads so_stateids
without clp->cl_lock. nfs4_put_stateowner() unhashes that openowner under
cl_lock and then frees it, so a concurrent EXCHANGE_ID with mismatched
creds can use-after-free the nfs4_openowner.

BUG: KASAN: slab-use-after-free in client_has_state+0x10a/0x140
  fs/nfsd/nfs4state.c:3718 client_has_openowners()
  nfsd4_exchange_id
  nfsd4_proc_compound
  nfsd_dispatch
  svc_process

Take clp->cl_lock while client_has_openowners() walks the openowner
list.

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: KVM: SVM: use-after-free of nested page table pointer on AMD INIT reset
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

KVM: x86: Unconditionally reset MMU context when emulating INIT

Force an MMU reset when emulating an INIT even if paging was already
disabled, as the MMU page role includes guest_mode (L2), i.e. an INIT while
L2 is running with CR0.PG=0 will result in KVM running L1 with a stale MMU
context.

Alternatively, the reset could be scoped strictly to paging being enabled
or L2 being active, but SMM is also encoded in the page role.  Even though
it _should_ be impossible for the vCPU to be INIT'd while SMM is active,
there's zero value in not handling SMM.  At that point, the only scenario
where KVM _doesn't_ need to reset the MMU context is on an INIT with the
vCPU running in Real Mode or Unpaged Protect Mode, and while INIT in those
modes is somewhat common, it's far from a hot path and re-initializing the
MMU is not expensive, especially when the role isn't changing (KVM elides
most of the re-configuration in that case).

Note, like the Fixes commit, this bug only affects nested SVM as INIT is an
unconditional intercept on VMX, i.e. it's impossible to emulate INIT while
L2 is active.

Temporarily keep the guest TLB flush when CR0.PG is being cleared even
though it is fully redundant with the flush that is emitted on all INIT
events (KVM itself only does RESET when a vCPU is being created, i.e. when
CR0.PG must be '0').

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: Information disclosure via out-of-bounds read during ksmbd compound response padding
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ksmbd: fix out-of-bounds read when padding the final compound response

Compound response handling pads the last response of a compound to an
8-byte boundary by growing the final iov and the RFC1002 length.
smb2_allocate_rsp_buf() allocates exactly response_sz. A command can
fill the response buffer to within 7 bytes of its end, for example a
QUERY_INFO whose output is bounded only by the space left. The padding
can then run past the allocation, and ksmbd_tcp_writev() reads those
bytes when it sends the response.

  BUG: KASAN: slab-out-of-bounds in _copy_from_iter+0x744/0x10e0
  Call Trace:
   _copy_from_iter+0x744/0x10e0
   tcp_sendmsg_locked+0x2290/0x3f80
   ksmbd_tcp_writev+0x10c7/0x1ab0 [ksmbd]

Allocate room for the padding when the request is a compound, as
smb2_read() and smb2_read_pipe() do for their payloads. response_sz is
unchanged, so commands still fill only up to it, and kvzalloc() zeroes
the padding.

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: Information disclosure via improper ASID allocation in KVM SVM
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

KVM: SVM: Trigger new ASID allocation in both VMCBs on pCPU switch

When the pCPU where the VMCB was most recently used is switched, reset
the ASID generation in both VMCBs, triggering new ASID allocation for
the immediate VMRUN as well as the next VMRUN on the other VMCB.

The ASID is shared between vmcb01 and vmcb02, and gets flushed on every
nested transition. However, since pCPU tracking is done per VMCB, it is
possible for one VMCB to allocate a new ASID when migrated to a new
pCPU, and then the other VMCB reuses that ASID on the old pCPU. This can
result in the same ASID being used by multiple vCPUs on the old pCPU.

Example scenario:
- vCPU runs on pCPU A, vmcb01 is active, asid=1.
- vCPU migrates to pCPU B, vmcb01 pCPU changes, new asid=2.
- Another vCPU runs on pCPU A and allocates asid=2 as well.
- vCPU migrates back to pCPU A, and then switches to vmcb02 before it
  runs again with vmcb01.
- No pCPU switch is detected for vmcb02, so VMRUN is done with asid=2.
- Two vCPUs end up using asid=2 on the same pCPU.

Keep the VMCB dirtying to the active VMCB only. Clean bits are tracked
by a pCPU for each VMCB, so do not unnecessarily dirty a VMCB if its
pCPU does not change.

Additionally, initialize the tracked pCPU for vmcb02 to -1 on nested
enablement as hardening, so that a new ASID allocation is always
triggered when nested is disabled and re-enabled.

No performance regression was noticed when overcommitting L1 vCPUs in L0
(to force rescheduling), pinning L1 <-> L2 vCPUs, and running CPUID in a
tight loop bouncing between 2 vCPUs in L2.

An alternative (and perhaps more proper) fix would be tracking the ASID
per-VMCB instead (e.g. [1]). However, that's a more involved change, and
it would result in having different ASIDs for L1 and L2 without actually
properly maintaining them. It would probably work because all TLB
flushes target the current VMCB, and the other VMCB is always flushed on
nested transitions, but the code ends up in an arguably more fragile
state. Punt a proper clean fix to an incoming (and overdue) overhaul of
SVM's ASID usage [2].

[1] https://lore.kernel.org/lkml/20250205182402.2147495-2-yosry.ahmed@linux.dev
[2] https://lore.kernel.org/kvm/20260728003557.1136583-1-yosry@kernel.org

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: Denial of Service via oversized SUNRPC GSS proxy token
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

SUNRPC: fix oversized GSS proxy token copy

gss_read_proxy_verf() allocates one page per token chunk, but it copies the
entire linear head of an RPC request into in_token->pages[0]. A UDP datagram
can leave more than PAGE_SIZE bytes in the linear head, so a large
RPCSEC_GSS INIT token overwrites following pages.

Copy the linear head in page-sized chunks before switching to the request
page array. The linear head itself can span multiple pages.

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: sunrpc: Authentication bypass via integer underflow in deferred RPC handling
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

SUNRPC: Copy the deferred RPC Call from the head buffer

svc_defer() snapshots the RPC Call for replay once a pending cache
upcall resolves. It copies the Call starting (rq_arg.len -
head[0].iov_len) bytes before head[0].iov_base, a back-up that once
covered a transport header. No transport has had one since commit
983084b2672c ("SUNRPC: Remove svc_rqst::rq_xprt_hlen"), so the two
lengths are meant to be equal.

An RPCSEC_GSS Call breaks that assumption. Unwrapping the integrity
service truncates rq_arg.len by the length of the trailing checksum,
and unwrapping the privacy service leaves rq_arg.len short by an
amount the client sets with trailing bytes after the wrap token.
Neither adjusts head[0].iov_len. Both lengths are size_t, so the
subtraction underflows and the copy starts past head[0].iov_base.
Every deferred integrity Call replays a shifted snapshot.

A deferred replay skips GSS verification, so a shifted snapshot runs
as an authenticated Call. With the privacy service the offset is
client-chosen. A forged Call placed in that window, naming another
user's GSS context handle, runs under that identity.

Copy the Call from head[0].iov_base. Refuse to defer a Call whose
length runs past the head buffer, so the copy cannot read out of
bounds.

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: Denial of Service via concurrent session slot replays in nfsd
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

nfsd: don't modify a session slot when replaying its cached reply

nfsd4_sequence() claims a session slot by setting NFSD4_SLOT_INUSE
under nn->client_lock. A reply served from the slot's reply cache does
not claim it, and that distinction lived only in cstate->status, which
nfsd4_sequence() set to nfserr_replay_cache. Commit cc028a10a48c
("NFSD: Hoist status code encoding into XDR encoder functions") moved
nfsd4_proc_compound()'s cstate->status assignment below the out:
label, and the replay path's goto out was the one path that relied on
skipping it. The test in nfsd4_sequence_done() therefore no longer
identifies a replay, and every replay now stores its reply and clears
NFSD4_SLOT_INUSE as though it owned the slot.

NFSD4_SLOT_INUSE is the interlock: check_slot_seqid() rejects every
sequence id for a slot that is in use, before replay_matches_cache()
runs. A replay never sets it, so two replays can be in flight on the
same slot at once. One can read slot->sl_cred under nn->client_lock
while the other's completion frees and rebuilds it from the XDR
encoder without that lock. Two completions can also collide with each
other and release the same group_info twice. free_svc_cred() leaves
cr_uid, cr_gid and cr_flavor intact, so the reader passes every
earlier test in same_creds() and dereferences a NULL cr_group_info.
From a 6.12.91 production server:

  BUG: kernel NULL pointer dereference, address: 0000000000000004
  CPU: 63 UID: 0 PID: 39015 Comm: nfsd
  RIP: 0010:same_creds+0x38/0xa0 [nfsd]
  RDX: 0000000000000000
  Call Trace:
   nfsd4_sequence+0x6a8/0x910 [nfsd]
   nfsd4_proc_compound+0x345/0x670 [nfsd]
   nfsd_dispatch+0x100/0x220 [nfsd]
   svc_process_common+0x311/0x700 [sunrpc]
   svc_process+0x131/0x1c0 [sunrpc]
   svc_recv+0x7ef/0x9c0 [sunrpc]
   nfsd+0xa3/0x100 [nfsd]
  Kernel panic - not syncing: Fatal exception

Since v6.14 a live session's slot table can shrink, and the unowned
store becomes a use-after-free write. nfsd4_sequence() defers the
shrink while a slot is in use, but it tests NFSD4_SLOT_INUSE, which a
replay does not set, so free_session_slots() can kfree() the slot the
replay still holds in cstate->slot.

Record the claim in cstate->slot_owned when nfsd4_sequence() accepts a
request and test that in nfsd4_sequence_done(), so only the request
that claimed the slot updates its cached reply and clears
NFSD4_SLOT_INUSE. svc_generic_init_request() zeroes the compound
response before each request, so the flag starts clear.

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: Information disclosure via out-of-bounds read in SMB client
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

smb: client: bound POSIX lock data area by response length

CIFSSMBPosixLock() receives a TRANS2 response whose server-provided
DataOffset and DataCount are not required by validate_t2() to describe an
interval inside the response. A server can therefore make the client read a
cifs_posix_lock beyond the response buffer and return those kernel bytes
through F_GETLK.

Use smbCalcSize() to obtain the full response length after any multipart
TRANS2 reassembly, then reject data areas that extend past it before
dereferencing them.

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: out-of-bounds memory write in SMB Direct via buffer length underflow
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

smb: smbdirect: fix buffer length underflow in RDMA transfers

When a remote buffer descriptor is larger than the remaining local
buffer, smbdirect_connection_rdma_xmit() clamps its length and sets
buf_len to zero. The common accounting code then subtracts the clamped
length from buf_len, causing it to underflow. If another descriptor
follows, the loop processes it with a wrapped remaining length and
includes memory beyond the local buffer in the RDMA transfer.

A client can trigger an out-of-bounds kernel write with an SMB WRITE
request, or an out-of-bounds kernel read with an SMB READ request, by
supplying multiple RDMA buffer descriptors with an oversized descriptor
before the last one.

Remove the premature assignment to buf_len. Subtracting the clamped length
already consumes the remaining buffer, so the next iteration stops and
only descriptors within the local buffer are used to build work requests.

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: ksmbd: Denial of Service via out-of-bounds write during directory name conversion
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

smb: server: size directory name conversion buffer correctly

A 2048-byte ASCII directory name needs 4098 bytes when converted to
UTF-16, including the terminator. ksmbd_convert_dir_info_name() caps
its allocation at PATH_MAX and writes past the end of that buffer.

Allocate space for one UTF-16 code unit per input byte plus the
terminator. Use kmalloc_array() to check the size calculation.

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: Unauthorized file replacement in OverlayFS via copy-up of removed files
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ovl: do not copy up a dentry that was removed

A change to a removed file through an open descriptor replaces whatever
has its old name in the upper layer.

Copy up must only create a name in the upper directory, never replace
one. After an unlink, an rmdir or a rename over a lower dentry, a
dentry that an open file keeps alive still has its old parent and name,
but in the upper directory that name is now a whiteout or a new object.
ovl_copy_up_workdir() renames the copy over it, which brings back the
removed object and destroys whatever took its name.

An unprivileged user opened a lower FIFO and unlinked it, root created
a file at that name, and fchmod on the old descriptor replaced the file
of root with the FIFO.

Fix this by looking up the target name of the rename in
ovl_copy_up_workdir() with LOOKUP_EXCL, so that copy up fails with
-EEXIST if the name is taken, as copy up with O_TMPFILE already does
when it links the copy to the name.

[amir: use LOOKUP_EXCL instead of relying on d_unhashed()]

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: Use-after-free in OverlayFS during directory copy-up
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ovl: set OVL_WHITEOUTS before publishing the upper dir

Listing a directory while it is copied up causes a use-after-free of
the readdir cache.

A merge directory must never be iterated as a real upper directory:
that mode frees the cache in OVL_I(inode)->cache without looking at
its refcount, while files opened in merged mode still use it.
ovl_copy_up_workdir() publishes the upper dentry before it sets
OVL_WHITEOUTS, and ovl_dir_open() samples both without a lock, so an
open between the two stores finds the upper directory and takes it
for a real one.

With a delay between the two stores, an unprivileged process that
listed a directory during its copy-up saw only "." and "..", and its
next getdents freed the readdir cache of another descriptor.

Fix this by setting OVL_WHITEOUTS before ovl_inode_update(), so that
ovl_dir_reset() agrees with ovl_dir_open(), and by testing
OVL_TYPE_MERGE() of the path type in ovl_dir_open(), so that an open
that observes the upper dentry never iterates a merge dir as a real
dir, regardless of the order in which it observes the flag.

[amir: test OVL_TYPE_MERGE() instead of smp_rmb() in ovl_dir_open()]

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: Denial of Service via use-after-free in NVMe target authentication
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

nvmet-auth: serialize access to DH-HMAC-CHAP state to fix UAF

A REPLY AUTH_SEND command can derive a dhchap_skey key while a
concurrent AUTH_RECEIVE command observing this REPLY state executes
the failure path and frees that key. The REPLY command then continues
and writes into freed memory, causing a use-after-free. KASAN reports
it as:

  BUG: KASAN: slab-use-after-free in __sha256_final
  Write of size 4 at addr ffff88800359c540
  ...
  nvmet_auth_sq_free (drivers/nvme/target/auth.c:237)
  nvmet_execute_auth_receive (drivers/nvme/target/fabrics-cmd-auth.c:621)

Add a mutex to each submission queue to serialize authentication
commands and timeout handling. Unlock the mutex before completing
requests and ignore outdated timeout callbacks. Limit timeout delays
to prevent immediate expiry on 32-bit kernels.

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: rtl8723bs: memory corruption via crafted protected Wi-Fi frames
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

staging: rtl8723bs: fix protected RX frame validation in decrypt path

The RX software decrypt path mishandles crafted protected frames from a
malicious AP in two ways:

1) decryptor() never checks that a protected frame is long enough to
hold the 802.11 header plus the per-cipher trailer.  All of
rtw_wep_decrypt(), rtw_tkip_decrypt() and rtw_aes_decrypt() compute

	length = hdr.len - hdrlen - iv_len;

and act on the result, and recvframe_chkmic() similarly computes

	datalen = hdr.len - hdrlen - iv_len - icv_len - 8;

for TKIP (the 8-byte Michael MIC is not accounted for in icv_len).
A frame shorter than hdrlen + iv_len + icv_len (+ 8 for TKIP) underflows
these unsigned subtractions, turning into a ~4 GiB iteration count in
aes_decipher()/arc4_crypt()/rtw_seccalctkipmic() or a ~4 GiB crc32_le()
length, causing out-of-bounds reads/writes of up to ~4 GiB starting from
the rx skb.  Reject such frames in decryptor() before touching the IV;
this covers all three ciphers and the TKIP MIC check, and also keeps the
unconditional iv[3] access within the frame.

2) validate_80211w_mgmt() keeps using the frame - two memcpys through
the stale rx_data pointer and a pkt_len update - before checking
whether decryptor() returned NULL.  On decrypt failure (e.g. a unicast
protected deauth/disassoc/action frame with a bad MIC, which this path
always software-decrypts) the skb has already been freed, so this is a
use-after-free read/write, and the caller's error path frees the frame
a second time, drifting free_recvframe_cnt.  Bail out immediately when
decryptor() fails, freeing the temporary mgmt_DATA buffer first.

Discovered by Atuin - Automated Vulnerability Discovery Engine.

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: Denial of Service via use-after-free during MPTCP request socket cloning
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mptcp: hold MP_JOIN msk ref when cloning reqsk

TCP request migration clones pending request sockets with
inet_reqsk_clone().  For MPTCP MP_JOIN requests this byte-copies
subflow_req->msk, but the clone does not own a reference.

The original and cloned requests can consequently drop the same msk
reference, leaving one request with a dangling pointer.  This manifests as
a KASAN slab-use-after-free in subflow_req_destructor():

  BUG: KASAN: slab-use-after-free in subflow_req_destructor (net/mptcp/subflow.c:45)
  Write of size 4 at addr ff1100010e008d40 by task swapper/0/0
  CPU: 0 UID: 0 PID: 0 Comm: swapper/0 Not tainted 7.2.0-rc5-00353-gc27e36054537 #10 PREEMPT(full)

  Call Trace:
   subflow_req_destructor (net/mptcp/subflow.c:45)
   subflow_v4_req_destructor (net/mptcp/subflow.c:694)
   __reqsk_free (net/ipv4/inet_connection_sock.c:906)
   reqsk_timer_handler (include/net/request_sock.h:137 net/ipv4/inet_connection_sock.c:1147)

  Allocated by task 10014:
   sk_prot_alloc (net/core/sock.c:2246)
   sk_clone (net/core/sock.c:2488)
   mptcp_sk_clone_init (include/net/sock.h:1848 net/mptcp/protocol.c:3564)
   subflow_syn_recv_sock (net/mptcp/subflow.c:883)
   tcp_check_req (net/ipv4/tcp_minisocks.c:934)

  Freed by task 0:
   slab_free_after_rcu_debug (include/linux/kasan.h:235 mm/slub.c:2677 mm/slub.c:6439)
   rcu_core (kernel/rcu/tree.c:2645 kernel/rcu/tree.c:2897)

  Last potentially related work creation:
   kmem_cache_free (mm/slub.c:2638 mm/slub.c:6377 mm/slub.c:6504)
   __sk_destruct (net/core/sock.c:2289 net/core/sock.c:2391)
   sk_destruct (net/core/sock.c:2419)
   __sk_free (net/core/sock.c:2430)
   sk_free (net/core/sock.c:2441)
   mptcp_close (include/net/sock.h:2020 net/mptcp/protocol.c:3399)
   inet_release (net/ipv4/af_inet.c:442)

  The buggy address belongs to the cache MPTCP of size 2968
  The buggy address is 128 bytes inside a freed 2968-byte region

A non-NULL subflow_req->msk means that the request owns one reference. The
third ACK can concurrently transfer the original request reference to the
child and release it, so taking an unconditional hold on the copied pointer
is unsafe.

MPTCP sockets use SLAB_TYPESAFE_BY_RCU and all current inet_reqsk_clone()
callers run in an RCU read-side critical section. Document and
lockdep-check that calling-context requirement.  Read the pointer from the
original request and acquire a reference only if it is still live.  Use
refcount_inc_not_zero_acquire() so the subsequent ownership validation
cannot be reordered before the try-get, then re-read the original request
to verify that it still owns the same msk. If either check fails, clear the
clone pointer; otherwise its normal destructor balances the new reference.
Mark the ownership-transfer store with WRITE_ONCE() to match the lockless
reads.

The following patch completes the clone fixup for MP_CAPABLE token
ownership. Both patches carry the same Fixes tag and are required for
stable backports.

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: Use-after-free in KVM PowerPC Book3S HV via virtual-mode HPT hypercalls
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

KVM: PPC: Book3S HV: Add SRCU protection for virtual-mode HPT hcalls

The virtual-mode HPT hcall handlers (H_ENTER, H_REMOVE, H_BULK_REMOVE,
H_CLEAR_REF, H_CLEAR_MOD) call into book3s_hv_rm_mmu.c, which accesses
memslots via kvm_memslots_raw().  kvm_memslots_raw() uses
rcu_dereference_raw_check() to bypass SRCU lockdep annotation checking.
This is safe in real mode because the entire guest entry/exit is wrapped
in srcu_read_lock/unlock inside kvmppc_run_core() and
kvmhv_run_single_vcpu().

However, since commit 6165d5dd99db ("KVM: PPC: Book3S HV: add virtual
mode handlers for HPT hcalls and page faults"), these same handlers are
also executed in virtual mode via kvmppc_pseries_do_hcall(), which runs
after SRCU has already been released on guest exit.

A concurrent KVM_SET_USER_MEMORY_REGION deletion or move can therefore
call synchronize_srcu_expedited() — which does not wait for this thread —
and then kfree(slot) and vfree(slot->arch.rmap) while the hcall handler
still holds a raw pointer to the memslot.  lock_rmap() then writes to
freed vmalloc memory, leading to use-after-free and memory corruption.
Because kvm_memslots_raw() suppresses lockdep checks, this race is
entirely silent.

Fix this by factoring out the 7 HPT hcall handlers (H_REMOVE, H_ENTER,
H_READ, H_CLEAR_MOD, H_CLEAR_REF, H_PROTECT, H_BULK_REMOVE) into a
helper function, kvmppc_pseries_do_hpt_hcall(), and wrapping its call
site in srcu_read_lock(&kvm->srcu) / srcu_read_unlock(&kvm->srcu, idx).
Targeting only the HPT hcalls avoids wrapping non-HPT hcalls that sleep
(such as H_CONFER, H_REGISTER_VPA, H_PAGE_INIT) or handlers that already
acquire SRCU internally (such as H_RTAS).

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: Denial of service via use-after-free in Wacom HID driver
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

HID: wacom: Fix Use-After-Free in wacom_intuos_pad

wacom_intuos_pad() accesses wacom->shared->touch_input locklessly
inside the interrupt handler context.  If the Touch sibling device
is disconnected, wacom_remove_shared_data() clears 'touch_input'
outside any lock, creating a Time-of-Check to Time-of-Use (TOCTOU)
race condition where a preempted reader in interrupt context
dereferences the freed pointer, leading to a Use-After-Free.

Resolve this by introducing RCU protection for the touch_input
pointer:

 - Annotate 'touch_input' in wacom_shared struct with __rcu
 - Wrap all lockless readers in wacom_wac.c with guard(rcu)() and
   rcu_dereference() using a unified wacom_report_touch_mute()
   helper
 - Update writers in wacom_sys.c using rcu_assign_pointer()
 - Call synchronize_rcu() in wacom_remove_shared_data() to ensure
   all active RCU readers have finished before the input device is
   freed

Also wrap wacom_set_shared_values() and touch/pen assignments in
wacom_add_shared_data() inside the wacom_udev_list_lock to serialize
concurrent probe assignments, and verify that 'shared->touch == hdev'
before setting touch_input to prevent concurrent sibling probe state
desynchronization.

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: ksmbd: privilege escalation via session ID mismatch in encrypted SMB requests
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ksmbd: verify transform SessionId matches the decrypted header

When an encrypted request comes in, the decryption key is picked by
the SessionId in the transform header, but the request is then
authorized under whatever session the decrypted inner header names.
Nothing ever compares the two, so on a connection with more than
one session a client can get a request decrypted with one session's
key and run it as another session. Encrypted requests are exempt
from signing too, so a valid AEAD tag is the only proof of session
identity, and it is checked against the wrong session.

MS-SMB2 says the server must check that the transform SessionId
matches the one in the decrypted SMB2 header and treat a mismatch
as a protocol error. Add that check in __handle_ksmbd_work() after
decryption, before dispatching: the message has to be at least one
fixed SMB2 header, the first operation must not set
SMB2_FLAGS_RELATED_OPERATIONS and its SessionId must match the
transform SessionId, and every following non-related operation in
a compound chain must carry the same SessionId. NextCommand
offsets must be 8-byte aligned and stay inside the message; the
bounds check is done by subtraction so it cannot wrap.

When the decrypted payload is a compression transform, the
existing decompression step runs first and the decompressed SMB2
message is checked instead, since a compression transform header
carries no SessionId.

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: ksmbd out-of-bounds read via pipelined negotiation requests
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ksmbd: wait for negotiation before receiving another PDU

The receive thread queues a request and can read the next PDU before
the negotiation worker finishes. While need_neg is set, the next PDU
can cause ksmbd_init_smb_server() to replace conn->ops. A pipelined
SMB2 request can therefore make the worker handle an earlier, shorter
SMB1 request with SMB2 operations and read beyond its buffer.

An SMB1 multi-protocol negotiate may be followed by an SMB2 NEGOTIATE
that changes conn->ops again. Wait for work queued while the connection
is new or needs negotiation to complete before reading another PDU.
This keeps the operations stable for both stages of negotiation without
changing when need_neg is cleared.

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: out-of-bounds memory write in iommufd via missing bounds check in IOVA bitmap
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

iommufd/iova_bitmap: Ensure that iova_bitmap_set() handles the full IOVA

Generally userspace is going to step the dirty bitmap through the IOVA
space. However if the bitmap ends in the middle of a large PTE this is
problematic. The first step will clear the dirty bit and report dirty to
the end of its bitmap while the second step will see the clear'd dirty and
report clean for the start of the bitmap. If it happens this ends up
losing dirties.

Further this function is missing bounds checking so if this does happen
ther is a good chance it will write memory beyond what the userspace was
expecting.

Return an error code if this illegal condition happens.

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: Denial of Service via use-after-free in SCTP socket migration
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

sctp: hold shkey across socket migration

sctp_sock_migrate() transfers queued DATA skbs from the old socket to the
new one. skb_orphan() invokes sctp_wfree() during that transfer and drops
the skb-owned shared-key reference.

If userspace has removed that key from the association, this can be the
final reference. The following sctp_set_owner_w() then dereferences the
freed chunk->shkey while trying to take the new owner reference.

Take a temporary shared-key reference before orphaning the skb and release
it after the new owner has taken its reference. This preserves the selected
authentication key throughout the ownership transfer.

Bug found and triaged by OpenAI Security Research and
validated by Trail of Bits.

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: Ceph: out-of-bounds write via oversized inline data
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ceph: clamp the inline data length in ceph_fill_inline_data()

The MDS decides how much inline data to attach to a reply, and the
client parses inline_len without any upper bound: ceph_decode_need()
only verifies that the message actually carries that many bytes.
ceph_fill_inline_data() then copies the data into a single folio
with no length check, so a malicious or buggy MDS returning more
inline data than the folio can hold writes past its end.

Clamp the length to folio_size() so both callers, handle_cap_grant()
and fill_inode(), are covered.

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: hypervisor memory corruption via AMD IOMMU device table out-of-bounds read
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

iommu/amd: Force device table to maximum size

IOMMU can perform out-of-bounds read of the device table entry (DTE)
that is adjacent to the last DTE and falls outside the device table.
For example, if the device table can hold 0 to N-1 entries, then the
IOMMU can be made to fetch the Nth entry, which falls outside the
device table.

The device table is owned by the hypervisor (HV) and is assigned in 4KB
pages that are contiguous in system physical address (SPA). If the
out-of-bound DTE falls on a guest-owned page, then the guest can exploit
this bug to setup malicious table walks to corrupt HV pages and/or bring
down the system. Note that this bug does not manifest when the device
table size is set to its maximum size of 2MB.

Therefore, force the device table size to the maximum 2MB on affected
processors. These are CPU family 0x17 (Zen1/Zen2) through family 0x1a
(Zen5/BRH).

This is a mitigation for CVE-2024-21963.

kdump reuses the previous kernel's device table only when the size
encoded in the IOMMU device-table register matches
pci_seg->dev_table_size. A mixed rollout disagrees: the unpatched
kernel uses the IVRS-derived size and the patched kernel uses 2MB,
so __reuse_device_table() rejects the table. On SNP-capable IOMMUs
that rejection panics the kdump kernel. Kernels that both have this
patch agree on 2MB and reuse succeeds. Update the production kernel
and the crash kernel together.

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: Denial of Service via use-after-free in MPTCP endpoint listeners
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mptcp: pm: kernel: use RCU to free endpoint listeners

mptcp_pm_nl_create_listen_socket() starts the TCP listener directly
instead of going through mptcp_listen(). It consequently misses setting
SOCK_RCU_FREE on the parent MPTCP socket.

tcp_child_process() can invoke the listener's subflow_data_ready()
callback without holding the MPTCP parent lock or a reference to the
parent. An authenticated MP_JOIN racing with endpoint teardown can
therefore access the parent after its last reference has been dropped.
The ADD_ADDR error path can also close an already published listener.

Set SOCK_RCU_FREE before __inet_listen_sk() publishes the TCP listener,
matching mptcp_listen(). This protects the parent on every subsequent
close path, including a failed endpoint addition.

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: Use-after-free in MPTCP via TCP Fast Open on MP_JOIN subflows
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mptcp: do not use Fast Open on MP_JOIN subflows

tcp_fastopen_create_child() hands the SYN packet itself to
subflow_syn_recv_sock(). For an MP_JOIN request this takes the
fatal fallback: the cloned child is destroyed and handed back with
drop_req flagged, but tcp_fastopen_create_child() does not check
the flag and queues it, so accept() can expose the freed child.

MP_JOIN cannot use Fast Open: data on a subflow requires the
completed HMAC exchange (RFC 8684, sec. 3.2). Refuse it (only the
TFO path passes a SYN skb here) and let tcp_conn_request() fall
back to the regular MP_JOIN handshake; also strip the Fast Open
cookie from MP_JOIN SYN/ACKs.

[ Moving code to avoid clearing TS and consolidating checks. ]

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: Memory corruption via integer truncation during TLB range flushing
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm/mmu_gather: fix flushing ranges with 4 GiB or larger

__tlb_adjust_range() takes the size of the range which has to be flushed
as an unsigned int. Its callers, tlb_flush_{pte,pmd,pud,p4d}_range(), get
and pass an unsigned long. Consequently, a range that is 4 GiB or larger
gets truncated, possibly to 0.

On arm64 with hugetlb, a 64k kernel can have 16 GiB hugetlb folios
mapped contiguously at the PMD level and flush them when unmapping, and a
16k kernel can flush 64 GiB PUDs through tlb_unshare_pmd_ptdesc(). So
at least these two scenarios are affected.

Fix it by flushing the proper range instead of the truncated one by
properly using "unsigned long" for range_size.

Fix generated by an LLM and sent by Josef Bacik in private.

[ david: use two-tab indent, simplify description ]

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: Memory corruption via integer overflow in GUP-fast
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm/gup: check for overflow when converting nr_pages to bytes in GUP-fast

The overflow check in gup_fast_fallback() only covers the addition to
start. The preceding nr_pages << PAGE_SHIFT can already have truncated
the length on 32bit.

Users such as RapidIO's rio_dma_transfer() can derive such page counts
from a 64-bit userspace length.

Let's just check_shl_overflow() to reject any such overflow with
-EOVERFLOW early.

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: Out-of-bounds write in GUP-fast via zero page count
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm/gup: fix out-of-bounds write for nr_pages == 0 in GUP-fast

With nr_pages == 0, GUP-fast still enters its page table walk and can
write past the caller's page array. The old end <= start check caught
empty ranges, but was replaced with an overflow check.

Users such as OrangeFS can pass a zero page count derived from a
userspace-supplied length. So let's return zero for nr_pages == 0 before
starting the walk, just like GUP-slow.

Fix generated by an LLM and sent by Chris Mason in private.

[ david: simplify description ]

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: XFS: information disclosure via improper pNFS layout range validation
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

xfs: clamp the pNFS layout range to the maximum file size

xfs_fs_map_blocks() lets two bad layout ranges through. An offset of
2^63 or more is negative and passes "offset > limit". A length above
the limit, such as NFS4_UINT64_MAX, wraps "offset > limit - length"
and stays unclamped. With NFS4_UINT64_MAX, a read layout is built from
an uninitialized mapping.

Reject a negative offset and one at the limit, and clamp the length.
This needs "xfs: cap the block count of xfs_iomap_write_direct() at one
extent".

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: xfs: Denial of Service via invalid pNFS LAYOUTCOMMIT range
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

xfs: refuse a pNFS LAYOUTCOMMIT of a range without blocks

A client can commit a hole in a LAYOUTCOMMIT, because nfsd does not
check the extents against its layouts. xfs_iomap_write_unwritten() then
allocates written blocks there. A large hole overruns the block
reservation and shuts XFS down. A small one exposes stale data.

Refuse such a range with -EIO, using XFS_BMAPI_CONVERT_ONLY.

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: privilege escalation via missing TLB flush in khugepaged
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm/khugepaged: flush deferred unmaps before dropping a failed folio

collapse_file() can fail its reference-count or dirty-folio check after
unmapping with TTU_BATCH_FLUSH.  Both paths put back the isolated folio,
then unlock it and drop the lookup reference before reaching the common
try_to_unmap_flush().

The page-cache reference does not keep the folio stable once the lock is
released.  Another collapse can replace and free it.  With its PTEs
already gone, that collapse cannot flush the first task's per-task TLB
batch, and retract_page_tables() skips short or unaligned VMAs.  A CPU can
therefore retain a user translation to the freed folio.  This has been
reproduced with unprivileged MADV_COLLAPSE on a memfd.

Flush at out_unlock while the lookup reference and folio lock are still
held.  The common flush continues to cover the accumulated pagelist on
both success and rollback, preserving batching on successful collapses.

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: Use-after-free via integer overflow in IP fragment reassembly
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

inet: frags: limit the truesize of a reassembly queue

The truesize of fragments in a reassembly queue is only bounded by
the per netns ipfrag_high_thresh sysctl, which has no upper limit.

inet_frag_reasm_finish() sums the truesize of all fragments in an int.
If this sum reaches 2^32, it wraps, and the final sk_wmem_alloc
adjustment of the socket owning the reassembled skb can cancel its own
reference, leading to a use-after-free of this socket.

This can be triggered from an unprivileged user/network namespace,
raising ipfrag_high_thresh and using padded TUN packets, which keep
a large truesize after being trimmed by ip_rcv_core().

Track the sum of the truesize of fragments in each queue, and refuse
a fragment that would make it bigger than INT_MAX / 2. Callers kill
the queue on this error. This bound is far above the needs of
legitimate traffic.

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: Denial of Service via unterminated iSCSI session identifier
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

scsi: target: Verify the iSCSI ISID is null-terminated

iscsi_parse_pr_out_transport_id() returns the ISID of a FORMAT CODE 01b
TransportID as a pointer into the PERSISTENT RESERVE OUT parameter list,
lowercased in place and never null-terminated.  spc4r37 Table 508 requires
the field to be null-terminated, but a non-conforming initiator can omit
the NULL; when the ISID ends at the end of the received buffer, the pointer
is not a C string.

The registration code still consumes it as one: strcmp() in
__core_scsi3_locate_pr_reg() and in the REGISTER AND MOVE path, and
snprintf("%s") in __core_scsi3_do_alloc_registration(), which also reads
its first 8 bytes unconditionally with get_unaligned_be64() - a NUL check
does not bound that read.

When the parameter list spans more than one page, transport_kmap_data_sg()
maps it with vmap(), and the over-read walks off the end of the mapping
into the vmalloc() guard page and oopses.  Reproduced with a PR OUT
REGISTER + SPEC_I_PT parameter list of exactly 8192 bytes whose final
TransportID carries a 12-byte ISID without a terminating NUL:

  BUG: unable to handle page fault for address: ffffc9000138c000
  RIP: 0010:strcmp+0xc/0x30
  Call Trace:
   __core_scsi3_locate_pr_reg+0xd3/0x120 [target_core_mod]
   core_scsi3_decode_spec_i_port+0x8fc/0x13a0 [target_core_mod]
   core_scsi3_emulate_pro_register+0x73c/0x900 [target_core_mod]
   ...
   iscsi_target_rx_thread+0xef/0x1d0 [iscsi_target_mod]

With a single-page parameter list the buffer is a kmap() direct mapping, so
the over-read continues into the physically adjacent page instead of
faulting.  snprintf("%s") then copies whatever follows the ISID in memory
into pr_reg_isid, and PR IN READ FULL STATUS reports the registration back
to any initiator, turning the over-read into an info leak of kernel heap
contents.  Reproduced with a 4096-byte parameter list whose last
TransportID ends at the end of the buffer with a 4-byte ISID and no NUL,
interleaved with I/O to populate adjacent pages: the READ FULL STATUS
response returned the ISID as "0xleak" followed by raw bytes that were not
part of the parameter list.  The snprintf() into
pr_reg_isid[PR_REG_ISID_LEN] caps the echoed ISID at 15 characters, so at
most 11 bytes past the buffer are leaked per command, but the PR OUT
command is not rate limited.

Any initiator that can send PR OUT to an iSCSI-exported LUN can trigger
either variant, including a guest via vhost-scsi.

Require 8 bytes to remain after the ",i,0x" separator, and a NUL inside the
rest of the descriptor, before the ISID pointer is returned.  REGISTER AND
MOVE fails with TCM_INVALID_PARAMETER_LIST; on SPEC_I_PT no target port
claims the malformed TransportID, and the command fails the same way.

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: sctp: Denial of Service via missing chunk padding check in sctp_init_cause()
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

sctp: account for chunk padding in sctp_init_cause()

sctp_init_cause() accepts a chunk when skb_tailroom() can hold the
cause header and the payload. sctp_addto_chunk() then writes 0-3
bytes of padding before that header so the chunk stays 4-byte
aligned. The check does not include the padding, and the following
skb_put() calls skb_over_panic() from softirq.

Count the padding sctp_addto_chunk() is about to write. The cause
length on the wire stays the header plus the payload.

Found by LLM inspection, triggered and tested the fix.

Vulnerabilities.Title: kernel: kernel: Out-of-bounds write via oversized 9p virtio mount tag
Vulnerabilities.Description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

9p/trans_virtio: reject mount tags longer than NAME_MAX at probe

p9_virtio_probe() reads a 16-bit mount tag length (tag_len) from the
device config and kzalloc()s tag_len + 1 bytes for chan->tag with no
upper bound. A malicious or compromised host can present a tag of up to
65535 bytes; that tag is later copied into the single-page sysfs buffer
by p9_mount_tag_show() (memcpy(buf, chan->tag, tag_len + 1)), a
host-controlled out-of-bounds write of up to ~64 KiB past the PAGE_SIZE
attribute buffer.

Reject an overlong tag at probe time. A 9p mount tag is a name-like
identifier, so bound it by NAME_MAX (255): that limit is independent of
the sysfs/seq_file page size and is far above any legitimate mount tag,
which keeps p9_mount_tag_show() safe at the root without hard-coding a
seq_file implementation detail.

Vulnerabilities.Title: brace-expansion: brace-expansion: Denial of Service via stack exhaustion from crafted brace patterns
Vulnerabilities.Description: The brace-expansion library generates arbitrary strings containing a common prefix and suffix. Prior to 1.1.19, 2.1.5, 3.0.7, and 5.0.10, crafted brace patterns can exhaust the native stack in parseCommaParts because parseCommaParts recursively processes the remainder once per brace group and uses push.apply to pass every element of a very large comma-part array as a function argument. Patterns containing many comma-separated brace groups trigger the recursive path, while the large array triggers the argument-array path without deep recursion. These paths cause recursive and argument-array native stack exhaustion before max or maxLength can limit output, potentially terminating the Node.js process in a process-terminating denial of service. This issue is fixed in versions 1.1.19, 2.1.5, 3.0.7, and 5.0.10.

Prior to 1.1.20, 2.1.6, 3.0.8, and 5.0.11, deeply nested brace groups cause expand_() to recurse once per nesting level at comma-member and single-set expansion sites, exhausting the native stack before output limits can apply and potentially terminating the Node.js process. expand_ performs uncontrolled recursion for nested brace alternatives and single-part sets. deeply nested brace groups supplied as an untrusted pattern. expand_ is affected. expand is affected. Comma members is affected. Single set is affected. native stack exhaustion during nested sub-expansion. process-terminating denial of service. This issue is fixed in versions 1.1.20, 2.1.6, 3.0.8, and 5.0.11.

Vulnerabilities.Description: brace-expansion through 5.0.6 is vulnerable to denial of service. The expand() function exhibits exponential-time complexity in the number of consecutive non-expanding '{}' brace groups. An attacker who passes a crafted string to expand(), directly or transitively, can cause significant CPU consumption and event-loop blocking. The max option does not mitigate this, as it bounds the output size rather than the recursion work.

Vulnerabilities.Title: brace-expansion: Brace-expansion: Denial of Service via memory exhaustion in expand() function
Vulnerabilities.Description: brace-expansion through 5.0.7 is vulnerable to denial of service via memory exhaustion. The expand() function limits the number of results with a max option (default 100,000) but does not bound the length of each result string. By chaining multiple brace groups, an attacker keeps the result count under the limit while making each result progressively longer, so total memory scales with both count and string length until the process hits a fatal, uncatchable out-of-memory error. About 7.5 KB of input ('{a,b}'.repeat(1500)) crashes a default Node.js process. Any application that passes attacker-influenced strings to brace-expansion.expand() - directly or transitively via minimatch / glob brace patterns - can be crashed by a small request. Fixed in 5.0.8 by adding a maxLength option (default 4,000,000) that bounds accumulated output and intermediate arrays.

The fix for CVE-2026-14257 is bypassed by the vulnerability. This issue is fixed in versions 1.1.18, 2.1.4, 3.0.6, and 5.0.9.

Vulnerabilities.Title: ip-address: ip-address: Inconsistent IP address parsing leads to Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) and trust-boundary bypass
Vulnerabilities.Description: ip-address is a library for parsing and manipulating IPv4 and IPv6 addresses in JavaScript. Prior to 10.3.1, Address4 accepts an octet written with a leading zero and decodes it as decimal, while the WHATWG URL host parser, inet_aton, and getaddrinfo all decode a leading zero as octal. The library and the network stack therefore disagree about which host a string names. new Address4('012.0.0.1') reports correctForm() of 12.0.0.1 and isPrivate() of false, but fetch('http://012.0.0.1/') connects to 10.0.0.1. An application that builds a network trust-boundary decision on these checks, for example a filter intended to block Server-Side Request Forgery, or SSRF, will classify an internal target as external and allow the request. The defect is in the parse gate rather than in any one classifier, so every consumer of Address4 inherits it: isPrivate(), isLoopback(), isLinkLocal(), isCGNAT(), isInSubnet(), isHostInSubnet(), and correctForm() are all computed from the mis-decoded octets. This issue is fixed in version 10.3.1.

Vulnerabilities.Title: picomatch: Picomatch: Regular Expression Denial of Service via crafted extglob patterns
Vulnerabilities.Description: Picomatch is a glob matcher written JavaScript. Versions prior to 4.0.4, 3.0.2, and 2.3.2 are vulnerable to Regular Expression Denial of Service (ReDoS) when processing crafted extglob patterns. Certain patterns using extglob quantifiers such as `+()` and `*()`, especially when combined with overlapping alternatives or nested extglobs, are compiled into regular expressions that can exhibit catastrophic backtracking on non-matching input. Applications are impacted when they allow untrusted users to supply glob patterns that are passed to `picomatch` for compilation or matching. In those cases, an attacker can cause excessive CPU consumption and block the Node.js event loop, resulting in a denial of service. Applications that only use trusted, developer-controlled glob patterns are much less likely to be exposed in a security-relevant way. This issue is fixed in picomatch 4.0.4, 3.0.2 and 2.3.2. Users should upgrade to one of these versions or later, depending on their supported release line. If upgrading is not immediately possible, avoid passing untrusted glob patterns to `picomatch`. Possible mitigations include disabling extglob support for untrusted patterns by using `noextglob: true`, rejecting or sanitizing patterns containing nested extglobs or extglob quantifiers such as `+()` and `*()`, enforcing strict allowlists for accepted pattern syntax, running matching in an isolated worker or separate process with time and resource limits, and applying application-level request throttling and input validation for any endpoint that accepts glob patterns.

Vulnerabilities.Title: sigstore: Sigstore: Unauthorized certificates accepted due to ignored `certificateOIDs` verification option

This issue is fixed in version 4.1.1.
